title: Senior GIS Developer – Range Mapping Lead
description:
Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking a Senior GIS Developer to lead the production of federal species range maps for a high-priority data integration program. You will produce range maps for marine and anadromous taxa in compliance with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), facilitating iterative review cycles with government SMEs and coordinating formal government sign-off.

The Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

Work Location: Remote

Day to Day Responsibilities:

Lead species range map production, producing complete range maps for all marine and anadromous taxa in full compliance with the FWS Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).

Obtain and review the FWS Range Mapping SOP at or before project kickoff.

Conduct spatial data aggregation and normalization of range data from cloud data platform outputs, applying CRS transformations and spatial format standardization.

Validate spatial intersects against authoritative geographic layers, addressing dynamic habitat boundaries and overlapping Critical Habitat designations.

Facilitate iterative range map review cycles with both FWS Ecological Services and NOAA Fisheries (National Marine Fisheries Service) SMEs, incorporating feedback and producing revised map versions.

Produce QA documentation for each individual range map, ensuring all maps meet SOP acceptance criteria before submission for government sign-off.

Coordinate FWS Ecological Services sign-off on the Range Map Set deliverable.Support the development of updated range maps post-production as part of operational handoff documentation.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelors degree and 8 years professional experience, or a Masters degree and 6 years professional experience, or an Associates degree and 10 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 12 years’ professional experience.

U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance; all work must be performed within the United States.

Extensive GIS experience with a focus on species range mapping or federal environmental applications.

Direct experience with FWS Range Mapping SOP or equivalent federal range mapping standards.

Proficiency in ArcGIS, QGIS, or equivalent GIS platforms.

Proficiency in Python for GIS automation and spatial data processing, including ArcPy or equivalent scripting libraries.

Proficiency in SQL for querying and validating spatial data within cloud data platforms.

Experience with coordinate reference system transformations and spatial data normalization.

Experience conducting spatial intersect validation and Critical Habitat analysis.

Strong QA documentation skills for geospatial deliverables

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with NOAA Fisheries marine or anadromous species range data

Familiarity with Databricks or cloud data platforms for spatial data retrieval

Experience coordinating formal government deliverable approvals

GISP certification or equivalent

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Bellevue, WA, USA
description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

Excellent communication skills

Bonus

Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.

And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

title: Staff Product Designer
description:
Hi 👋 I'm Elvin, Head of Design at Pinpoint.

We're a high growth HR tech company building software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire, and onboard the right talent. Today we have a strong foundation in place: a mature product, rapid growth, strong product market fit, and happy customers.

Inside Pinpoint sits a part of the product most ATSs don't have: background checks, right to work, reference checks, one way video interviews and the credits and billing that power them. We call it Marketplace. It's the squad behind the revenue that scales with how much customers use us, and an important strategic bet towards continued growth.

For the past two quarters I've been its designer, its PM and the Head of Design at the same time. The next phase is harder than what we've already shipped, and it needs someone whose whole job it is, which is why we're hiring a Staff Product Designer.

You'll be the only designer on the Marketplace squad, working alongside our Head of Commercial Product (the squad's PM), our Tech Lead, a Senior Product Engineer, and our Head of Roadmap Engineering.

The fine print

100% remote. You can be based in the UK, Portugal, Spain or Poland, working UK hours, with a few in person team meetups a year. We're headquartered in Jersey with a team of 100 across the UK, EU and US.

The product is a set of status driven workflows: a check gets ordered, a vendor or a regulator decides what happens next, and the design has to handle every outcome, including the ones that fail. Our third party vendors set what's possible and the compliance rules are fixed, so you'll spend as much time understanding how a vendor actually behaves as you do in Figma.

AI is how we work, not a tool we're trialling. I ship my own PRs through Claude Code now, and I hadn't shipped one 3 months ago. You don't need to have done that yet, but you do need to be using AI across your work today and to want to learn.

There's no research function. Decisions have been quick and under pressure for a while. We want someone who can make a good call fast and who also pulls the squad toward research backed judgement as the norm.

Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions.

What you'll do

Own design for every usage based feature in Pinpoint, end to end: from the first conversation with a vendor or customer, through the spec and the design, to shipped and measured.

Ship the next phase of Pinpoint Checks: DBS update service with automated routing, rechecks, sending check data to downstream systems, decision and audit flows, and the UK high compliance checks that follow.

Turn credits from something customers are given into something they understand and use. Credit visibility, self serve costing and in platform credit management are being scoped now and they are yours to design.

Shape Marketplace product strategy with the PM going into 2027, then execute on it. Discovery here is shared between you and the PM, not handed to you.

Write the plan into the ticket before anything is built: the decisions made, the edge cases covered, the questions closed, so an engineer (or you) can build it with Claude without a second round of questions.

Prototype in code where it beats Figma, submit your own PRs for small front end fixes, and QA what ships.

Be the person Support, Sales and Legal come to when a check is stuck or a customer asks what a vendor does with their data. You'll know the domain better than almost anyone in the company within 90 days.

Bring Marketplace work to weekly design crit and feed new patterns (status cards, order flows, decision recording) back into Thumbtack, our design system.

What you'll bring

Experience designing complex B2B software products alongside a PM and engineers, with shipped work to show for it. Owning an area as the sole or lead designer is a plus

Startup or scale up experience and the mentality that comes with it: small teams, few handoffs, and a willingness to do whatever the product needs that week

Hands on work designing around constraints set by someone else: a regulator, a compliance rule or a third party vendor's API. Background screening, identity, fintech, payments, insurance and legal are the obvious homes for it, and comparable complexity elsewhere counts

Multi state workflows in the portfolio, such as orders, cases, applications and checks, where the system decides the next step and the design has to handle the moments when it can't

Familiarity with what changes at enterprise scale: permissions, configuration, multiple personas, and flows that hold up at 10 users and at 10,000

Daily use of AI across the whole job rather than only to produce screens faster, covering research, testing, investigating bugs, prototyping and documenting, plus the technical depth and appetite to learn to ship small PRs with Claude Code

Production ready UI craft that clears a high bar, shown in the portfolio

Ownership of the call when the data isn't there: deciding, explaining the reasoning, owning the outcome, and solving the problem in front of you whether or not it is strictly a design problem. Over time, pulling the squad towards research backed judgement as the norm

Fluency in commercial outcomes, so margin, adoption and conversion get discussed as naturally as flows and components

Bonus points for HR tech or ATS experience, and for credits, billing or usage based pricing

You may not enjoy this role if

You want a research team, a brief and a backlog handed to you. Here you write the brief.

You're waiting to see how the AI thing plays out before changing how you work.

You'd rather own the design system or lead a team. This is an IC role on one squad, and Thumbtack governance stays with me.

Your portfolio is agency work or consumer apps only. Marketplace serves enterprise customers ordering checks at volume, and the panel will test for it.

What we offer

We want Pinpoint to be the best place you've ever worked, somewhere you feel valued, supported and excited to grow. Here's what you get:

Comprehensive healthcare: excellent medical, dental and vision coverage for you and your family

Unlimited holidays: take the time you need to rest and recharge

Mental health support: unlimited, immediate access to professional counselling via Spill

Retirement contributions: 401k or pension contributions depending on your location

Remote first: work where you're most productive, with flexibility and trust as the default

Equity with real upside: share in the long term value you help create

Fully paid parental leave: up to 16 weeks of paid leave for new parents

Learning budget: annual funds for courses, books or anything that supports your growth

A detailed overview of our benefits is here.

What you're wondering

What does success look like in the first 90 days? By 30 days you can answer a Support question about a stuck check without me. By 60 you own one of the Q4 items end to end with the plan written into Linear. By 90 I'm out of Marketplace standups and you're the named design owner on the Marketplace roadmap.

What tools do you use? Figma, Thumbtack (our design system in Figma and Storybook), Claude and Claude Code, Linear, Fibery, PostHog, Notion and Slack. The product is Rails and React with TypeScript.

title: Retail Pharmacy Account Manager, Walmart - Southeast US (Secondment - 12 Months)
description:
WHY PATIENTS NEED YOU

Everything we do, every day, is in line with an unwavering commitment to the quality and the delivery of safe and effective products to patients. Our science and risk-based compliant quality culture is innovative and customer oriented. Whether you are involved in manufacturing, testing, or compliance, your contribution will directly impact patients.

WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE

The Retail Pharmacy Account Manager (RPAM) is responsible for developing durable business, deepening collaboration with Retail Pharmacy Field Leaders and growing appropriate use of Pfizer Primary Care Retail Pharmacy products. This is accomplished by identifying shared objectives, aligning resources, and deploying innovative solutions to achieve targeted business results. The RPAM’s primary focus is to ensure access to the Pfizer retail pharmacy portfolio through the development of productive relationships with Retail Pharmacy field leaders to support mutually aligned goals through projects and educations that drive operationalization. Additionally, the RPAM will engage diverse local stakeholders, combining innovative thought, entrepreneurial business acumen, and account management skills. This candidate will need to work with highly matrixed organizations at Pfizer and its Retail customers. This position reports to the National Pharmacy Business Director (NPBD) and must collaborate closely with the Retail Trade Account Director (TAD), Sales and Account colleagues, Marketing & CCG, Medical and Legal and Compliance to plan and implement activities to achieve national, regional and district Pfizer goals and objectives.

HOW YOU WILL ACHIEVE IT

Customer & Account Management

Initiate and cultivate relationships with key retail pharmacy field leaders (decision makers and influencers) within the target customers such as Divisional Vice Presidents or equivalent, Retail Pharmacy Regional & District Leaders, Clinical Directors, Field Clinical Trainers, Field Operations, and other field pharmacy leaders outside the HQ offices who implement chain HQ direction to implement retail pharmacy-based programs.

Leverage Pfizer’s value proposition to create mutually beneficial business opportunities that result in action and outcomes.

Identify, connect and communicate multiple insights from various stakeholders to develop a plan of action that is mutually beneficial to Pfizer and the customer.

Seek out opportunities for synergy and collaboration to achieve both Pfizer and Retail Pharmacy customer goals through active and transparent customer planning.

Develop a tailored account management approach to each account based on their needs and adapt in response to evolving markets.

Prioritize retail customers opportunities and projects to maximize impact; leveraging all available internal data sets and stakeholder maps (to include Watchtower) input to optimize decision making.

Train and compliantly share externally-facing performance data with approved Retail Pharmacy Field Leaders.

Use customer-facing Population Health Discovery Tool (PHDT) to share geographic & demographic immunization opportunities.

Conduct expert account planning and practice effective project management using Pfizer Account Management resources (i.e. Valkre, etc.).

Implement and measure impact of customer-aligned Projects and Educations.

Identify & prioritize top Retail areas to progress the Operationalization process and track the progress of these targeted areas (Communication, Education, Patient Identification, Execution, and Stocking).

Employ strong pre-account management planning, effective presentation to focused and productive questions, as part of effective solutions-oriented project plans.

Generate sustained immunization initiatives with Retail pharmacy field leaders by successfully aligning Pfizer RC-approved resources to a customer’s immunization programs.

Use latest RC-approved educational content and resources to address needs of customers.

Implement pull through with effective project management to include field leader education and patient identification through workflow engagement tools.

Facilitate internal sharing of chain best practices in patient identification, workflow, and counseling.

Analyze and monitor key market trends, competition, past customer interactions, and other market data to maximize effectiveness of each account interaction.

Complete Full Account Management Curriculum Training, as well as Retail Pharmacy specific training.

Execute marketing programs across customer segment and present RC-approved materials to deliver value added messaging in a compelling manner; developing and executing projects that are strategic in nature and may have near, mid, and long-term market and business impact.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Operate in a team environment that encourages innovative ideas and a culture of collaboration and teamwork. Be adept at creating a vision for the future and be able to create a pathway to help optimize the customer’s vaccination opportunities in a compliant and engaging way.

Align with Retail Trade Account Director (TAD) to ensure appropriate understanding of, and support for Retail Pharmacy goals (i.e., brand and customer).

Collaborate with local Sales ABMs to navigate a complicated internal matrix that aligns their HSS teams to drive pull through.

Drive customer centric focus overarching account value versus product specific, understand and address what influences prescribing and purchasing (or stocking) decisions.

Contribute to internal customer plans in collaboration with TAD. Impact and influence development of RPAM strategies by partnering with needed cross functional teams to compliantly shape efforts and deliver results.

Work with TAD to understand the strategic plan for each of the target customer, and the implications for how to prioritize and implement the plan in each geography.

Utilize organizational awareness skills and alignment of Pfizer's priorities to include appropriate Pfizer colleagues with a Retail Pharmacy to optimize value provided to the Customer and to Pfizer.

Provide the marketing and strategy teams with key geographic and customer specific insights that they can utilize in crafting new market-specific materials.

title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Evanston, IL, USA
description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

Excellent communication skills

Bonus

Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.

And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

title: Account Partner - Marketing Analytics
description:
Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.

At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.

Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.

The Role

Crossix is positioned at the center of big data, innovative technology, media, and life sciences. Our mission is to empower life sciences companies with the data and insights they need to drive DTC and HCP marketing effectiveness and, ultimately, better patient outcomes. As part of Veeva, the Crossix team offers the agility of a high-growth team with the stability of a global leader.

The Veeva Crossix Sales team is looking for a skilled Account Partner (Marketing Analytics) to drive sales within our media measurement and optimization business to Life Sciences companies. To be successful in this role, you must be strong at communicating across various business functions, organizational levels (including C-level), and brand marketing departments. Creativity, initiative, and the ability to work effectively within a growing team are critical. You are also someone who is humble, hungry, and smart – you put the success of the team ahead of your own; you have a relentless drive to do what it takes to succeed, and you find a way to overcome obstacles and solve business problems.

What You'll Do

Develop a thorough understanding of Crossix offerings, competitive advantages, and processes. Learn to articulate them persuasively to prospects and customers

Develop strong and mutually valuable relationships with new and existing customers

Manage pipeline with CRM tools for maximum efficiency and visibility, with carefully executed follow-up to closure

Work in close partnership with Client Services to manage successful client deployments and to ensure ongoing high client satisfaction, renewal, and deep penetration of customer organizations for incremental business

Keep current with industry trends; engage your customers, address their business challenges, and propose solutions

Requirements

Passionate about healthcare with a strong interest in pharmaceutical marketing. You feel a strong connection to our mission and will work hard to ensure customer success

As an educator and business consultant; you love teaching clients about how they could maximize their potential working with us.

Demonstrated development of meaningful partnerships with a diverse client base and proven track record as a trusted advisor to brands

Highly organized with a firm grasp of your business - you accurately log all sales activity and prospecting in SFDC with speed and accuracy

Understanding of the digital media/marketing landscape with the ability to credibly articulate strategic insights for clients that are based on data and research

A fast learner, you love to stay at the forefront of an ever-evolving industry

A creative problem solver - you stay cool under pressure and thrive in an atmosphere of change

At least 3 years experience in selling technology, marketing, pharma data/insights, or media solutions in the life sciences industry or closely related field

Proven track record of exceeding sales goals while contributing to the success of the team

Strong understanding of digital media and ad tech ecosystem

At least 5 years of overall business experience in sales, business development, or account management preferably in digital advertising, technology businesses, and healthcare data/consulting

Eagerness to work in a startup team environment that will be rapidly changing

BS or BA degree is required

Interviewing with Veeva

We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.

Follow the application process and submit your resume.

Within 3 days, you will receive a link to a personality assessment administered by a third party.

Once you complete the assessment, our team will review your full application package and follow up via email with our decision.

If moving to the interview stage, the process is as follows:

A conversation with the hiring manager

A practical case exercise

A final conversation with our group's Senior Leader.

Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision.

Perks & Benefits

Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance

Flexible PTO and company paid holidays

Retirement programs

1% charitable giving program

Compensation

Base pay: $80,000 - $300,000

The salary range listed here has been provided to comply with local regulations and represents a potential base salary range for this role. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range above or below, depending on experience and location. We look at compensation for each individual and base our offer on your unique qualifications, experience, and expected contributions. This position may also be eligible for other types of compensation in addition to base salary, such as variable bonus and/or stock bonus.

Veeva’s headquarters is located in the San Francisco Bay Area with offices in more than 15 countries around the world.

Our global footprint across Asia, Oceania, Europe, and the Americas enables us to run 24-hour follow-the-sun workflows, our professional translators and game developers continue to work on your project around the clock, delivering on even the most challenging timelines.

The team at Keywords Studios handle media localization and translation services for any project size, from indie to AAA games. The Project Manager will consistently meet or exceed client expectations by ensuring exceptional service, quality, and cost efficiency on every project. Working with clients, colleagues across different accounts and a broad spectrum of resources, the Project Manager is expected to develop and grow those relationships whilst achieving/exceeding the expected margins by providing creative, technical, and business solutions.

The PM is expected to manage projects of different sizes, genres and platforms and ensure their profitability, quality and on time delivery within the timeframe agreed with the client.

Work on projects, depending on workload and on the team’s needs.

Estimate and plan projects from start to finish, with built-in contingencies.

Work with the Senior Production Manager and global team to ensure that the project’s specific workflows and technical processes are well documented and regularly updated.

Work closely with the Solutions Team, the Senior Production Manager, and the client directly to understand the scope and requirements of each project.

Advise clients on best practices and agree on project processes and timelines.

Monitor and coordinate project processes (pre- and post-production plans, postmortems, resources, QA plans, risk mitigation plans, CAPAs, etc.) and collaborate with the teams in charge of those different areas of expertise.

title: Crop Insurance Adjuster
description:
As one of the leading writers of Federal Crop Insurance, AgriSompo North America combines industry experience, resources, capital and talent to deliver both traditional and innovative crop insurance and productivity tools to farmers, ranchers, insurers and agribusinesses in the United States. Our organization operates within a culture rooted in ethics, integrity and a belief that accountability, collaboration and agility are crucial to long-term success.

AgriSompo North America is a part of AgriSompo, Sompo International’s global agriculture platform. This platform is an integrated underwriting, technology and distribution platform delivering innovate insurance and reinsurance solutions to agriculture partners worldwide. Sompo International, AgriSompo’s parent company, is a global organization driven by its core values, a carrier that holds promise, trust and the commitment to protect. Through operating subsidiaries, Sompo International writes agriculture, casualty and other specialty, professional lines, property, marine/energy and aviation lines of insurance and catastrophe, property, casualty, professional lines and specialty lines of reinsurance.

As a leading provider of crop insurance and other agricultural risk management tools, we recognize that our success is derived directly from those whose contributions matter most: our people. AgriSompo North America has major offices in Lenexa, Kansas and Des Moines, Iowa as well as regional offices around the country. A shared commitment to integrity, accountability, collaboration and agility define our culture, and we strive to create exceptional value for our clients and shareholders and maintain AgriSompo North America as a desirable place to work.

Job Description

Are you looking for your next opportunity?

AgriSompo has a unique opportunity for a Crop Insurance Adjuster to join our Midwest team, supporting our Multi-Peril Crop Insurance (MPCI), Private Products, and Named Peril claims operations.

Location: This position will be based remotely in Kansas (West Central Kansas or Southwest Kansas). We strive for collaboration which is why we offer a work environment where our employees thrive and develop long lasting careers.

Our business, your impact, our opportunity:

What you’ll be doing:

Build and maintain professional relationships with the Area Claim Supervisor, policyholders, agents, and other adjusters

Record and transmit loss information to accurately determine potential damages in accordance to established loss adjustment procedures (FCIC, NCIS and Company)

Complete field inspections, read maps and aerial imagery, measure fields and measure storage bins

Utilize company software proficiently including daily monitoring of all company communications

Follow FCIS, State, and Company rules and regulations, policies, and procedures for MPCI and Private Products

Complete initial and ongoing training and certifications as required by FCIC and State Regulations

Explain adjusting procedures and related findings to the policyholder and agent

Perform fact-finding and investigate crop damage, record information, and transmit information to accurately determine potential indemnities

Willingness to learn new crops

What you’ll bring:

Preferred 2 years’ experience handling crop insurance claims

Required license and certification: CAPP certification and valid driver’s license with a satisfactory driving record and applicable State license

High school diploma or equivalent, or equivalent combination of education and experience with a Bachelor’s degree in agriculture preferred

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Basic mathematical skills (add, subtract, multiply, divide).

Effective interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills with the ability to interact with all levels of people within and outside the organization.

Ability to complete documentation requirements.

Ability to utilize analytical thinking; find facts and solve problems.

Ability to remain self-motivated and efficient.

Ability to work both in an office setting and outdoors in a farm environment.

Ability to work well both independently and within a team environment.

Ability to remain focused on exceptional customer service, both internally and externally.

Working knowledge of crop insurance regulations, policies, procedures and best practices.

Works effectively under pressure and able to work within tight deadlines.

Willingness to take initiative and work with minimal supervision.

Strong time management skills with ability to prioritize.

Physical Requirements & Work Conditions

Ability to lift/push/pull up to 50 lbs. occasionally; including ladders, bushels, ramps for off road vehicles.

Ability to walk in agricultural fields, up to 3 miles.

Ability to climb agricultural storage bins, up to 75 feet.

Ability to climb, crawl, stoop, kneel and balance.

Ability to climb ladders and perform work at significant heights.

Ability to perform work in confined spaces.

Ability to work outside in extreme weather conditions.

Ability to work in an environment with high dust levels around grain and other bulk products.

Ability to meet requirement of and utilize all applicable PPE, when applicable.

Ability to work extended hours, weekend, holidays and/or as needed.

Uses peripheral vision and depth perception for tasks being performed.

Environmental Conditions

The work environment described is intended to represent the typical conditions an employee may encounter while performing the essential functions of this role. The physical environment requires work in both indoor and outdoor settings, including exposure to varying weather conditions such as heat, cold, humidity, and dryness. Use of personal protective equipment is frequently required.

This role also involves up to 50% travel, primarily within a two-hour driving distance from the assigned home office. Occasional out-of-town travel may be necessary for trainings and meetings.

Actual compensation for this role will depend on several factors including the cost of living associated with your work location, your qualifications, skills, competencies, and relevant experience.

At Sompo, we recognize that the talent, skills, and commitment of our employees drive our success. This is why we offer competitive, high-quality compensation and benefit programs to eligible employees.

Our compensation program is built on a foundation that promotes a pay-for-performance culture, resulting in higher incentive awards, on average, when the Company does well and lower incentive awards when the Company underperforms. The total compensation opportunity for all regular, full-time employees is a combination of base salary and incentives that gets adjusted upfront based on overall Company performance with final awards based on individual performance.

We continuously evaluate and update our benefit programs to ensure that our plans remain competitive and meet the needs of our employees and their dependents.

Below is a summary of our current comprehensive U.S. benefit programs:

Two medical plans to choose from, including a Traditional PPO & a Consumer Driven Health Plan with a Health Savings account providing a competitive employer contribution

Pharmacy benefits with mail order options

The Data Science & Engineering organization's mission is to increase our speed, frequency, and acumen in making decisions at scale by instilling a data-influenced approach to building products. In Data Science & Engineering, you will build the macroeconomic models, simulation frameworks, and policy mechanics that scale Roblox’s virtual economy. By analyzing Robux currency dynamics, global pricing strategies, and developer exchange policies, your work will directly inform strategic decision-making, financial policy, and executive roadmaps on our road to connecting one billion users.

You will:

Develop, build, and refine macroeconomic models to forecast and monitor Robux money supply, velocity, inflation/deflation dynamics, and overall virtual economy health.

Model and inform comprehensive currency exchange policies, encompassing fiat-to-Robux purchase pricing, regional purchasing power (PPP) adjustments, and Developer Exchange (DevEx) rates, to balance global user participation, developer incentives, and long-term platform sustainability.

Design and run counterfactual simulations (e.g. causal inference frameworks, agent-based modeling) to evaluate the impact of proposed monetary policies, sink/faucet adjustments, and marketplace fee changes before execution.

Analyze sink and faucet dynamics across the platform to balance liquidity, optimize developer economy mechanics, and prevent systemic economic imbalances.

Partner closely with Product and Finance leadership to translate complex economic data into actionable policy recommendations and sustainable growth strategies.

Establish robust economic indicators and monitoring systems to track real-time macro-health metrics, liquidity risks, and structural shifts in user behavior.

Communicate complex strategic findings and macroeconomic trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders to directly influence company-level roadmaps and economic policy decisions.

Promote technical excellence in quantitative policy analysis, econometrics, and simulation methodologies across the broader Data Science and Engineering team.

5+ years of industry or research experience applying quantitative economic modeling, econometrics, or simulation frameworks to analyze policy, marketplace dynamics, or user behavior.

Deep expertise in quantitative methodologies including time series forecasting (e.g., VAR, state-space models), causal inference (e.g., synthetic control, diff-in-diff), structural macro modeling (e.g., DSGE), and counterfactual simulation techniques (e.g., agent-based modeling).

Proven track record working with large-scale transactional or platform data to analyze micro-level user behaviors and aggregate them into macro-level economic insights.

Demonstrated ability to lead project areas from scratch, translating ambiguous business and policy questions into rigorous quantitative frameworks and iterative research deliverables.

Strong communication skills to explain complex economic trade-offs, risk scenarios, and simulation results to non-technical stakeholders in Finance and Product leadership.

An Advanced Degree (MSc or PhD) in Economics, Econometrics, Quantitative Finance, Statistics, Operations Research, Physics, or a related quantitative field.

A systems thinker.

Curious and truth seeking.

A deep collaborator. You understand where your skills provide differential value and complement others, and how the strengths of others complement you.

title: Founding Operator
description:
About Babou

Brands use us to run more campaigns and more channel-specific creative without growing their production org or raising agency spend.

We are small and early. You would work directly with the founders, and you are applying to us directly rather than through a staffing agency.

About the role

Babou's founders need a right hand. We're looking for people that take on and close things out.

The job is one loop:

Fill the funnel, inbound and outbound, so we are never waiting on leads.

Close the loop on every lead. Nobody goes quiet because we forgot to follow up.

Onboard new customers and get their templates built and shipped.

Keep customers successful after launch.

Run the creative team doing the building: scope, dates, and follow-through.

Whatever is stuck this week is yours. A deal that went quiet, a customer missing a file, an artist running late. You don't escalate it. You pick up the phone that same day.

I want to hand you an outcome and then stop thinking about it.

"This deal stalled. Get it moving."

"Our onboarding is broken. Fix it."

"We need a system for this. Come back with one."

You work out what the actual problem is, make the calls you can make, flag the ones I have to make, and get the first chunk done before you bring it back to me.

This is probably not for you if

You need tasks specified before you can start

You are looking for a strategy or advisory role

You would rather coordinate work than do it

You wait for approval on reversible decisions

You need your responsibilities to stay inside a defined box

You think AI output is finished work

On AI

We are a slop-free startup.

AI makes output cheap, it has not made reviewing that output any cheaper. Handing us unfiltered, unreviewed, verbose AI output moves your work onto someone else's desk. That will get you fired.

Use AI constantly, to take on more than one person could. Read everything before it leaves your hands.

Backgrounds that tend to work

Your title matters much less to us than what you actually owned.

You ran a small agency or studio, where you sold the work and then shipped it

Former founder

Early employee at a startup where everyone did everything

You have already been a founder's right hand

If you have made payroll, chased an unpaid invoice, or sat across from an angry client, say so.

5+ years of work experience, at least 2 of them owning outcomes rather than tasks

Strong written English (C1+) and comfortable spoken English on a live call

Modern laptop with 24GB+ RAM

Fully remote

title: ML Researcher, World Models
description:
At Geolava, we bring AI to the physical world. We are building spatial intelligence systems by leveraging world models to simulate the evolution of the physical world over time. We continuously model real-world dynamics, simulate actions, and forecast their impact on assets.

We are backed by top-tier VCs and have been revenue-generating from day one. This is your opportunity to join as a founding team member to help define the future of spatial intelligence from the ground up.

We are looking for an ML Researcher to help build Geolava's world model for the built world: a system that perceives the current state of properties and infrastructure, learns how they change over time, and forecasts what comes next, whether the driver is time, a renovation, a new construction, or a hurricane. You will work from raw earth observation and property data all the way to a model that can reason about state, action, and future state, and you will decide how we measure whether it works.

This is a research role on a small team, and you will own real problems end to end: framing the question, designing the experiment, running it on real data at scale, and writing up what you learned. It is also a startup. Research that works here does not sit in a paper. It ships as a capability inside the product that property investors, lenders, and infrastructure owners use to make decisions.

Responsibilities (What You'll Do)

Design, train, and evaluate world models of the built environment that predict how assets change over time and in response to interventions and external forces.

Develop representation learning and predictive modeling approaches over multi-temporal aerial and satellite imagery, property records, and other physical and administrative signals.

Build rigorous evaluation for a domain with no public benchmarks: baselines, held-out temporal splits, calibration, and tests that distinguish genuine forecasting skill from leakage.

Run experiments on cloud GPUs with attention to throughput and cost, and turn results into clear, decision-ready writeups.

Work with the AI and engineering teams to take successful research into production as capabilities in Geolava's platform.

Stay current with the world-model, self-supervised learning, and generative modeling literature, and bring the ideas that matter into our work.

Your Background

World-model research experience. You have built or contributed to world models: learned dynamics models, latent predictive models, action-conditioned generation, or closely related work, in academia or industry. This is required.

PhD. You hold a PhD in machine learning, computer vision, or a closely related field.

Deep learning fluency. You are comfortable training large vision models, adapting foundation models efficiently, and diagnosing why a training run behaves the way it does.

Empirical rigor. You design experiments to answer questions, insist on proper baselines and splits, and are honest about what the evidence does and does not show.

Ownership. You are productive with ambiguous problems and small teams, and you drive work from idea through result without waiting for a roadmap.

title: Head of Sales
description:
About Slate

Slate is a commercial cleaning company serving clients nationwide. We work with businesses that care about the spaces they operate in — from boutique fitness studios and medspas to offices and commercial facilities. We're a growing team of 150+ and we're at the point where sales needs an owner. That's this role.

The Role

You'll be Slate's first dedicated sales hire, responsible for building and running the sales function end to end. This is a true full-cycle role: you'll own the pipeline from first touch to signed contract, and you'll design the systems and processes that make it repeatable as we scale.

Day to day, that means:

Owning our lead generation channels. Manage and optimize the channels that bring us leads — digital, referral, partnerships — and figure out which ones deserve more investment.

Running targeted outbound. Build prospect lists in our key verticals, run account-based outreach to decision-makers, and pick up the phone when that's what it takes.

Handling inbound. Respond to inquiries quickly and professionally, qualify them, and move the right ones forward.

Conducting discovery. Run discovery calls and video walkthroughs, understand each prospect's operational needs, and scope engagements we can deliver on — partnering with our NYC operations team for on-site walks.

Negotiating and closing. Structure proposals, negotiate contracts, and get deals signed.

Handing off cleanly. Transition new clients to account management so they're set up for a great first ninety days.

Building the function. Continue building our internal (using AI), define the process, track the numbers, and shape our sales strategy as we grow — this role is both hands-on and strategic.

Why This Role

Ground-floor ownership of an entire function, with direct access to the founder and leadership team.

A real product to sell: an established client base, strong service delivery, and room to grow in proven verticals

Your work will visibly move the company's trajectory — and your compensation will reflect it

Requirements

Who You Are

4+ years of B2B sales experience with full-cycle ownership — ideally selling services (facilities, cleaning, security, staffing, or similar recurring-revenue services)

Comfortable being a team of one: you can prospect in the morning, run discovery at noon, and refine the pipeline dashboard in the afternoon

Genuinely happy on the phone — this is a relationship business, and you'll spend real time talking to prospects, not just emailing them

Strong negotiator who can hold margin while building trust

Organized and systems-minded: you don't just close deals, you build the machine that closes deals

Familiarity with CRM tools and modern outbound tooling

Based anywhere in the US

Nice to have: experience selling to multi-location businesses (fitness, healthcare, retail, hospitality) or in commercial real estate–adjacent services.

Benefits

Compensation

We publish our full comp structure because we want you to see exactly how the money works before you apply.

Base salary — starts at $1,000/week, with an automatic, formula-based path to $2,000/week:

$1,000/week to start

$1,500/week once the accounts you've closed are adding $20K/month to Slate's active recurring revenue (each account active and paying for 60+ days)

$2,000/week when your accounts are adding $50K/month

Steps up the pay period after you hit the milestone — no annual review, no discretion. Once earned, your base never goes back down.

Uncapped commission on every account you close, paid monthly for the first 12 months of each contract, as the client pays:

7% on the first $10K of an account's monthly billing

3% from $10K–50K/month

1.5% above $50K/month

Our accounts range from ~$2K/month to $200K+/month in billing, so the earning ceiling is real: a seller sustaining a healthy close rate in our core verticals reaches six-figure total comp well within year one, with no cap above that.

Homeworking position.

You will explore and develop high-impact partnerships that put children at the centre and advance WVI’s strategic influence, with a particular focus on private and blended finance stakeholders, faith-based investment, environmental, social and governance and sustainable finance as vehicles for improving child wellbeing.

Capture learning from strategic partnerships and coalition engagement, translating insights into practical guidance for future private sector, faith-based investment and multi-stakeholder collaboration.

Regularly scan relevant influencing spaces where Field Offices and Support Offices are active, ensuring global partnering work remains grounded in locally led approaches.

title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Cary, NC, USA
description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

Excellent communication skills

Bonus

Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.

And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Athens, Greece
description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

Excellent communication skills

Bonus

Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Greece Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-55,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Chattanooga, TN, USA
description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

Excellent communication skills

Bonus

Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.
